Sepsis due to Escherichia coli (A41.51) secondary to acute pyelonephritis (N10)

Multiple sclerosis, relapsing-remitting (G35)
Neurogenic bladder (N31.9) with chronic intermittent self-catheterization
Major depressive disorder, single episode, moderate (F32.1)

History of Present Illness:
75 year old woman with relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis and neurogenic bladder managed with intermittent catheterization presented with 3 days of fever, rigors, right flank pain and vomiting. On arrival T 102.9 F, HR 118, BP 86/50, lactate 4.1, creatinine 2.3 from baseline 0.9. Urinalysis with pyuria and nitrites.

Hospital Course:
She met sepsis criteria and received 30 mL/kg crystalloid with blood pressure response, avoiding vasopressors. Empiric cefepime was started. Blood and urine cultures grew E. coli, pan-sensitive except ampicillin, and she was narrowed to ceftriaxone on hospital day 2. CT abdomen pelvis showed right pyelonephritis without abscess or obstruction. Fever resolved by day 3. Creatinine improved to 1.0 with fluids and holding metformin and lisinopril. Blood glucose was elevated to the 300s in the setting of infection; basal bolus insulin was used and she was transitioned back to her home regimen with the addition of glipizide. Neurology was notified; no signs of MS relapse. Mood was stable and sertraline continued.

Procedures: None.

Discharge Medications:
NEW: cefpodoxime 200 mg PO every 12 hours for 9 more days (total 14 days)
NEW: glipizide 5 mg PO daily with breakfast
RESUME: metformin 1000 mg PO BID
RESUME: lisinopril 10 mg PO daily, start 04/09/2025 if systolic BP above 120
CONTINUE: ocrelizumab infusion every 6 months per neurology (next due 06/2025)
CONTINUE: sertraline 100 mg PO daily
CONTINUE: oxybutynin ER 10 mg PO daily

Discharge Condition: Stable, afebrile, ambulating with walker at baseline.

Discharge Labs: WBC 8.9, Hgb 11.4, creatinine 1.0, glucose 164.

Follow Up:
PCP Dr. Fairweather within 7 days - repeat BMP
Urology Dr. Nakashima-Reyes in 4 weeks to review catheterization technique
Neurology as scheduled

Patient Instructions: Return for fever over 101 F, inability to keep fluids down, or decreased urination. Use a new sterile catheter each time.
